## About
G and M Auto Repair is on Rainier Ave S in Seattle. We do everyday work like oil changes, track down problems like blown fuses, and handle bigger jobs too. There's an autobody repair and paint booth in the back of the shop.
Customers tell us they appreciate that we take the time to explain things. When we find the problem, we'll show you the part and walk you through it so you understand what you're paying for. We're rated 5 from 132 Google reviews, and we'd like to earn your trust the same way.

## Services
- Oil changes and other jobs: Oil changes plus the basic and major jobs that keep your car running.
- Fuse and relay for charging ports: For one customer, we quickly replaced the fuse and the relay for the charging ports so they worked again.
- Autobody repair and paint: Body repair and painting in our paint booth at the back of the shop, with help matching the right color for your vehicle.
- Splash shield: We quickly fixed a broken splash shield for one customer.

## FAQ
Q: Are you open on Saturday?
A: Yes. We're open Saturday from 8:30 AM to 6:00 PM. We're closed Sunday.

Q: Can you match the paint color on an older vehicle?
A: One reviewer brought in an old pickup truck for paint, and the boss helped find the correct color to match the truck.

Q: Where is the shop?
A: We're at 3757 Rainier Ave S, Seattle, WA 98144.

## What customers say
- "I had taken my car to another mechanic 2 years ago because my charging ports and the rear defroster had stopped working. They told me that the fuse was fine and the problem was with the part in the console; because the part was integrated in the console, the entire center console had to be replaced and would cost at least $500 just for the part. Fortunately for me, I never ended up paying that money because they took months supposedly dealing with problems with their supplier while I called them once a week for updates because they never contacted me to keep me informed of the situation. I eventually moved and ended up taking my car to G and M Auto Repair. It was a world of difference; I was there barely an hour and they quickly identified that not only was a fuse blown, but there were 2 relays that were missing. He showed me the missing parts and the diagram in the lid of the fuse box that showed the part name and where it was supposed to be. Either someone removed it during a repair and forgot to put them back or they were intentionally removed to force me to spend more on repairs...I don't know which, but it's majorly concerning that the first mechanic either didn't notice the blown fuse and missing relays or was involved on the situation. G and M quickly replaced the fuse and the relay for the charging ports resulting in them immediately working again, the remaining relay for the rear window defroster needed to be special ordered and will hopefully be fixed in a week or so (they said they'd contact me as soon as the part was ordered in order to schedule an appointment for the repair). The entire hour of labor and replacement of 2 parts only cost me $198 (and some change). I'm truly grateful for how guick he was, the time he took to explain the problem and show me in detail to make sure I understood. His honesty and fair pricing was truly appreciated." (Amara McBride, 5/5)
